newsitem.title: USA: McLeod debt gains on Consolidated merger.
newsitem.headline: McLeod debt gains on Consolidated merger.

text.p: McLeodUSA Inc's outstanding debt forged two point gains on Monday after the company said it will merge with telecommunication company Consolidated Communications Inc, traders said.

McLeodUSA's $500 million in zero coupon debt traded at 64 on Monday morning, traders said, with the price since rising further to a 64-1/4 bid, 65 offer market. The debt was seen bid at 62-1/4 on Friday.

Douglas Conn, vice president and high-yield analyst at Lehman Brothers, said McLeodUSA, which operates in the mountain and midwestern states, will benefit from Consolidated's telephone operations and fiber optic links between urban areas in the midwest.

"This (merger) allows McLeod to buy facilities to buildout his super-regional network at a faster pace," Conn said, adding that chairman and chief executive Clark McLeod is also getting a cash-flow positive company with a long operating history.
McLeodUSA is a competitive local exchange carrier.

Under terms of the agreement, owners of Consolidated Communications will receive 8.49 million shares of McLeodUSA stock and $155 million in cash. McLeod will also assume $60 million of Consolidated long-term debt.

The merged company, to be called McLeodUSA Inc, would have revenues of about $400 million and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $6 million, McLeodUSA said in its announcement.
McLeodUSA shares were up 2-5/8 points at midsession to 27-1/8.
